messages.subject: Verdant v Calderhall - instructions to advise (merits & clause 11)
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Harriet,

Please find our instructions to advise on the merits of Verdant's claim and, in particular, the construction and reasonableness of clause 11 (cap + exclusion of consequential loss). The pleadings, the Wraysbury report and the key contemporaneous documents (the 18 March workshop minutes and the 22 March email on the energisation deadline) are in the enclosed bundle. We're particularly interested in your view on recoverability of the EPC LDs (640k) and lost revenue (284k).

Elena

Elena Marchetti
Associate | Whitfield Carter LLP

messages.subject: RE: Verdant v Calderhall - instructions to advise (merits & clause 11)
messages.plaintextBody:
Elena,

My written advice is attached. In short: liability looks strong (75-80%); the direct heads (1,551,200) should be recoverable in full and sit well within the cap; the 924k of EPC LDs and lost revenue are more finely balanced (55-60%) and turn on Calderhall's knowledge of the downstream deadline. The construction argument is stronger than the UCTA point. I'd push for early disclosure of the batch-release and root-cause records and a mediation after experts.

Happy to discuss on a call this week.

Harriet Stanford | Eldon Chambers
